title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not Grothendieck's own mathematics. It is page II.9 of an English typescript, with the script symbols (\mathcal M, \mathcal N, \mathcal O) filled in by hand. In the scan it is upside down, so it was evidently reused as scrap paper in the folder; the '15' in the corner is the archive page number. The surrounding folder pages are Grothendieck's French manuscript notes on rational equivalence of cycles on tori and on Albanese/Picard equivalences.

The typescript works with sheaves of modules on a ringed space (X, \mathcal O), where \mathcal O is possibly non-commutative, with restriction maps \alpha^U_V. It covers three points.
(1) There is a natural map \xi_{\mathcal M\mathcal N}: \mathcal{E}nd(\mathcal M)\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal{E}nd(\mathcal N) \to \mathcal{E}nd(\mathcal M\otimes\mathcal N). For finitely presented \mathcal M and \mathcal N, \mathcal{H}om commutes with taking stalks. When the stalks are finitely generated projective, the stalk map is the classical isomorphism End(P)\otimes End(Q) \cong End(P\otimes Q). Hence \xi is an isomorphism of sheaves.
(2) For a left \mathcal O-module \mathcal M, the dual \mathcal{H}om_{\mathcal O}(\mathcal M,\mathcal O) is made into a right \mathcal O-module by (f\cdot a)_V(m) = f_V(m)\,\alpha^U_V(a).
(3) The text begins defining \psi: \mathcal M^\vee\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal M \to \mathcal{E}nd(\mathcal M). It first defines \psi' on the presheaf tensor product \otimes' and then sheafifies; presumably \psi'(f\otimes m)(n) = f(n)m. The page breaks off before the formula.

This is standard preparatory material for proving that \mathcal{E}nd(\mathcal E) of a locally free sheaf of finite rank is an Azumaya algebra, and that tensor products of such algebras behave well. It reads like a student thesis or lecture notes on Brauer groups or Azumaya algebras over ringed spaces, of the kind written in the wake of Auslander–Goldman and Grothendieck's 'Le groupe de Brauer I'.
errors: The isomorphism claim needs the stalks to be finitely generated projective, i.e. \mathcal M and \mathcal N locally free of finite type. Finite presentation alone only gives the compatibility of \mathcal{H}om with stalks. The text does assume projectivity of the stalks, so the argument is correct as stated.
Typo in the typescript: 'by means fo the operation' should read 'by means of the operation'.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a page of someone else's routine English typescript on sheaves of modules, apparently reused upside down as scrap paper. It contains only textbook facts and no Grothendieck mathematics.
transcription_corrections: The scanned page is upside down; the transcription correctly reads it rotated.
The map's subscript looks like \xi_{\mathcal M\mathcal N} (handwritten script M and N), not \xi_{\mathcal N}. The same applies to the stalk map \xi_{\mathcal M\mathcal N,x}.
The hand-written '15' in the corner is the archive page number, not part of the text.
